name: Guggul
kitchenUse: Not a kitchen herb; taken only as purified guggul in tablets such as Yogaraja or Kaishore guggulu.

typicalUse.adultAmount: Only as a qualified practitioner advises; products and strengths vary
typicalUse.note: Raw guggul must be purified (shodhana) before use.

cautions.note: Avoid in pregnancy; it is traditionally said to stimulate the uterus.
Not enough is known; avoid while breastfeeding.
May affect thyroid hormones; avoid with thyroid disease unless your doctor agrees.
May act like oestrogen; avoid with hormone-sensitive conditions.
May slow blood clotting; stop two weeks before surgery.
Can cause itchy skin rashes when taken by mouth.

interactions.effect: May change thyroid hormone levels and the effect of thyroid medicines.
May add to the effect of blood thinners.
May reduce absorption of some heart medicines such as propranolol and diltiazem.

evidence.summary: Trials on cholesterol are conflicting; one well-run trial found no benefit and a small rise in LDL. Some small trials suggest help for knee osteoarthritis.

sources.title: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part I
